featured_reviews.name: Deepak Maurya
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a very concerning experience at Anuradha Gas Station (Indian Oil), JVLR Andheri East.

On 15 June 2026, I filled petrol and the staff initially told me the bill amount was around ₹3,491. I was surprised because I had observed the meter and expected the amount to be around ₹2,700. After questioning them, they produced a bill showing ₹3,391, and I ended up paying the amount through UPI.

Later, when I reached home and checked the receipt carefully, I noticed that the receipt time was 20:41, whereas my UPI payment was made at 21:13. This clearly indicated that the receipt did not belong to my transaction. I immediately returned to the petrol pump, and after discussion, the staff admitted it was a "mistake" and refunded the excess amount.

What makes this even more suspicious is that during a previous visit, I witnessed another customer arguing that petrol had not been filled into his vehicle despite being charged.

Such incidents raise serious concerns about transparency and customer trust. Customers should carefully verify the meter reading, receipt details, and transaction amount before making payment. The management and authorities should investigate these repeated complaints and take strict action if any fraudulent practices are found.

I have preserved the receipt and payment proof and will continue to raise this issue with the appropriate authorities if necessary.

Date of Incident: 15 June 2026
Location: Anuradha Gas Station, JVLR, Andheri East, Mumbai

#IndianOil #ConsumerRights #FuelFraud #Mumbai #PetrolPumpComplaint

featured_reviews.name: Meera Patel
featured_reviews.review_text:
Here’s a strong and concise social media post combining both incidents:

This is the SECOND suspicious incident I’ve faced at Anuradha Petrol Pump (Indian Oil), JVLR Mumbai.

Earlier this month, I asked for petrol worth ₹5000, but only around ₹4200 was filled while a higher bill was shown. After confronting them, the manager admitted the mistake and issued a corrected bill.

Again, day before yesterday, I asked for fuel worth ₹1000, but they initially filled only ₹200 and claimed the filling was complete. When I questioned why my fuel indicator had barely moved and demanded the manager, they quietly filled more petrol.

This pattern looks extremely unethical and misleading. Customers, especially women and senior citizens, should stay alert and always check the meter and fuel level carefully.

Requesting Indian Oil to investigate this petrol pump seriously before more customers get cheated.

featured_reviews.name: Dr Anuradha Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
I usually prefer filling petrol at Indian Oil petrol pumps, but yesterday I had a rather disappointing experience. While returning home, I stopped at this petrol station to fill fuel in my car.

The man filling the petrol suddenly started asking, “Where in UP are you from?” At first, we thought he was speaking to someone else, but when he repeated the question, Arvind — my brother’s friend who was driving — replied, “Varanasi.” After that, he continued asking more personal questions, and in the middle of the conversation, he suddenly said, “Auto cut ho gaya hai.”

We had asked for petrol worth ₹1005, but when I looked carefully, the meter had already shown two lines before the filling even started. He then claimed the machine had auto-cut at ₹840 and returned the remaining amount because I had already paid ₹1005 in advance. Even while returning the balance, the amount was ₹5 short.

What felt even stranger was that once we started driving, the fuel indicator in the car barely moved up. Only God knows what actually happened.

Overall, the entire experience left me feeling cheated and deeply disappointed. It is sad how, at times, people compromise their honesty and integrity for such small gains. Trust is something customers carry with them when they stop at a fuel station, and once broken, it leaves a very unpleasant feeling behind.

Ironically, my name is also Anuradha, and coincidentally, the gas station was called “Anuradha Gas Station.”

🚨 Beware of the Air Pump Scam! 🚨
Next time you stop to fill air in your tyres, stay alert. A common trick is happening at some air pumps:

💨 Air slowly leaks out…
⚠️ Then he tells you, “tyre is punctured.”

Right beside the pump, another person (part of the same scam) will quickly offer to “fix” it and charge ₹200–₹300 to replace the valve — even though nothing was actually wrong.

🛑 How to protect yourself:
• Watch closely while air is being filled
• Check the valve yourself before agreeing to any repair
• Don’t rush into paying for “quick fixes”
• If possible, fill air yourself

👉 Stay alert. Share this post to help others avoid getting scammed!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Located strategically near the Vile Parle airport area, this Indian Oil outlet is a frequent stop for many travelers and locals alike. While there are several things they get right, there are a few persistent operational issues that prevent it from being a top-tier station.

The Positives: Hospitality and Maintenance
The most impressive aspect of this pump is the conduct of the staff. In a city where fuel station employees are often rushed and dismissive, the team here stands out. They are polite, professional, and well-coordinated in managing the constant flow of vehicles, especially during peak airport hours.
Another huge benefit is the Free Nitrogen Air facility.
Most stations in Mumbai either have broken air machines or charge extra for Nitrogen.
Here, the machine is usually functional, and the service is free, which is a massive plus for vehicle maintenance and tire longevity.
The fuel quality also seems consistent, and I’ve never had an issue with the "zero-check" or the accuracy of the dispensing units.

The Major Drawback: Payment & Connectivity
The reason for my 3-star rating boils down to the frequent and frustrating payment failures. In a digital-first economy, being told "the server is down" is a significant inconvenience.

Digital Payment Reliability: On several visits, they have refused to accept Credit/Debit cards or UPI (Google Pay/PhonePe), citing server issues or machine connectivity problems.

The Cash Scramble: Since this pump is near the airport, many customers are on their way to a flight or have just landed. Not everyone carries enough cash for a full tank of fuel. Being told at the last minute that online payments aren't working creates unnecessary stress and delays.

Areas for Improvement
While the staff is doing their best, the management needs to prioritize their IT infrastructure.

Backup Systems: They should invest in a more stable internet connection or have multiple POS (Point of Sale) machines from different banks to ensure card payments always go through.

Advance Warning: If the server is truly down, there should be a prominent sign at the entrance so customers aren't caught off guard after the fuel has already been pumped.

Final Verdict
Go here for the polite service and the free Nitrogen, but always carry cash just in case. It’s a reliable station for fuel quality, but the recurring "server down" excuse for digital payments is a hurdle that needs to be fixed to earn back those extra stars.
